 Judgment

The appellant before this Court is a young man whose right hand has become dysfunctional owing to K.Santhosh vs Radhadevi on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14678509/
1 an injury he has suffered while he was traveling as a pillion rider in a motorcycle bearing Regn.No.TN 36 AD 1010.
The accident had taken place on 05.06.2016.
2.In the accident, he had suffered fracture to his right forearm, that however was corrected with a surgery.
It was then found that he had an issue with breichel plexus, a nerve that is responsible for the motor activity of the hand.
An attempt was made to surgically correct it.
On 22.03.2017, a surgery was performed at the Stanley Medical College Hospital and it was a failure.
Few months thereafter, to be precise on 12.01.2018, another surgery was tried by the Stanley Medical College Hospital namely, Contracuadeval C 7 Nerve Transfer surgery.

What in effect was attended by the surgeon was a small portion of the nerve in the four finger was removed and it was injected through the right thorax area into the right arm pit area and the idea was that this nerve will get connected with the remaining nerve in the right arm and start growing https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis over a period of time.
This surgery too ended in a total failure.
The consequence was that the entire motor activity of the right hand was lost to the victim.
To state it differently, his right has become dysfunctional permanently.
3.It is in these circumstances, the claimant approached the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, III Additional District Court, Erode seeking compensation in MCOP.No.36 of 2017.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The medical board Vide Ext.C.1 certificate assessed the permanent disability of the victim of the accident at 65%.

The Tribunal however, awarded compensation at Rs.3,000/- for every percentage of disability and arrived at a sum of Rs.1,95,000/- as compensation for permanent disability, to which it added medical expenses and compensation payable under certain non- pecuniary/conventional heads.

In all, it awarded a total compensation of Rs.3,35,450/- and the break-up is as below;

sentences.text: 5.The victim of the accident has appeared before the Court and it is he who explained the injuries and surgeries that he had undergone.

It may be stated that this young man was prosecuting his Bachelor's Decree in Political Science at the time when the accident had taken place and having passed it successfully, he had proceeded to do his Law.
He https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis explained that he wrote all his examination with the assistance of a scribe.
6.Heard both sides.

7.The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal has been singularly insensitive to the plight of this young boy, despite the fact the medical board has recorded his right hand is dysfunctional.
Secondly, it failed to grant adequate compensation under other conventional heads.

8.On seeing the unfortunate demonstration of the victim of the accident about the surgeries he had undergone, the learned counsel for the second respondent made a fair statement that it is a case were the disability must be treated as a functional disability.
9.The circumstances are ideally set for this Court to treat the disability of the victim as a functional disability.
Inasmuch as the right hand of this young man has literally become dysfunctional, it may affect his marital https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis prospects.

This Court is also informed that he is a right hander and his is now managing with his left hand.
10.On evaluation of the facts before this Court

, this Court considers it to be appropriate to treat the nature of disability suffered by the claimant/appellant as functional disability and determines the same at 50%.
11.This Court now fixes the notional monthly income of the victim of the accident at Rs.18,000/-, to which it adds another 40% towards future prospects of increase in income, applies 18 as the multiplier and arrives at a net sum of Rs.54,43,200/- and on reducing it to 50%, the sum awardable under the head of functional disability is determined at Rs.27,21,600/-.

The modified award will now read as below;

 Amenities  Grand Total 3,35,450/- 34,75,042/ Enhanced by  - 31,39,592/-
12.In fine, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed and the compensation is enhanced from Rs.3,35,450/- to Rs.34,75,042/-, together with interest at 7.5% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The second respondent/Insurance company is now required to deposit the sum now awarded by this Court, along with interest, less the interest payable for 1110 days, within a period of six (6) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

On such deposit, the appellant is https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis permitted to withdraw the award amount, now determined by this Court, along with interest and costs, less the amount if any, already withdrawn.
The appellant is directed to pay the necessary Court Fee, if any, on the enhanced award amount.
No costs.
